### PR [#2507](https://github.com/open-quantum-safe/liboqs/pull/2507) — Fix out-of-bounds read in HSS validate_signature_init

Norman reported that he had identified this issue as overlapping with one or more items in the private security-tracking repository. He was uncertain whether to address it via the public PR or through the private security workflow, and had been waiting for Douglas (who was on leave until Thursday) to clarify. The discussion surfaced a broader coordination issue (see below).

### Security advisory process and tooling

The discussion around PR #2507 revealed coordination friction in the current security-handling workflow:

- Norman found that he could see some security advisories (because he was tagged as a reviewer by Michael) but could not create branches on the private fix repos that GitHub automatically generates for each advisory — preventing him from directly committing proposed fixes. In at least one case he could not tell whether he had access to the fix repo or not, and resorted to pasting diffs in comments.
- Rodrigo observed that information about the same issue was appearing in multiple places (the public PR, the security advisory, the private tracking repo), making it difficult to know where to act and where to look.
- Michael clarified the intended model: the security team assigns reviewers per advisory topic (e.g. Norm for LMS/XMSS), and GitHub automatically creates a private fix fork. The access problem Norm encountered is likely a permissions configuration issue that Ryan can resolve.
- Rodrigo noted a remaining gap: the security process as defined covers OQS team members with GitHub presence, but does not yet specify who contacts external algorithm maintainers (who are the true owners of the upstream code) when a security issue affects their algorithm. He proposed that the TSC chair take on this coordination role by default, or appoint someone.

Agreed next steps: Norm will share the link to the advisory fix repo he could not access so that Rodrigo can raise the permissions issue with Ryan. For the public PR #2507, Norm and Rodrigo agreed that Norm should acknowledge the contributor's work, note that an independent fix is already in progress for the same issue, and either adopt the PR as the vehicle for the fix or proceed with the independent fix and credit the reporter — whichever is cleaner. All substantive discussion of open security issues will be centralised in the private security-tracking repository to avoid fragmentation.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Action (Norman):** Share the link to the inaccessible advisory fix repo with Rodrigo, so the permissions issue can be raised with Ryan.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Action (Norman):** Respond to [PR #2507](https://github.com/open-quantum-safe/liboqs/pull/2507) acknowledging the contributor, and coordinate with Rodrigo on whether to proceed via that PR or via the independent fix.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Action (Rodrigo):** Raise the fix-repo access issue with Ryan and, as a TSC agenda item, define who is responsible for contacting external algorithm maintainers when a security issue affects their upstream code.

## OQS-OpenSSL 3 provider

### OpenSSL master compatibility fix and re-enabling master CI ([PR #806](https://github.com/open-quantum-safe/oqs-provider/pull/806))

Rodrigo reported that OpenSSL has landed a fix for the provider-freeing / caching incompatibility that had been blocking the provider's CI against OpenSSL master ([issue #792](https://github.com/open-quantum-safe/oqs-provider/issues/792)). With that fix in place, PR #806 (re-enable OpenSSL master testing in CI) can move forward. Both Norman and Michael have approved it. A separate CI failure (CC compiler not found) is affecting all provider CI jobs at the moment; Michael quickly identified this as a job running outside the normal OQS CI container and offered to investigate. The team agreed to proceed with merging PR #806 once this CI issue is resolved.

On CI strategy for OpenSSL master, Michael proposed — and Norman and Rodrigo agreed — a caching approach: a scheduled job (daily or weekly) rebuilds OpenSSL master if new commits have landed and caches the result; all per-PR CI runs during that period test against the cached build rather than rebuilding OpenSSL from scratch on each push. This gives near-real-time feedback on master compatibility without making OpenSSL master the most expensive step on every PR. Rodrigo will close the existing [issue #807](https://github.com/open-quantum-safe/oqs-provider/issues/807) (homogenise CI across platforms) as out of scope and open a new, more focused issue to implement the daily cache approach.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Action (Michael):** Investigate the CC compiler not-found CI failure affecting oqs-provider and resolve it so PR [#806](https://github.com/open-quantum-safe/oqs-provider/pull/806) can merge.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Action (Rodrigo):** Close [issue #807](https://github.com/open-quantum-safe/oqs-provider/issues/807) and open a new issue to implement a daily cached OpenSSL master build for per-PR CI.
